steps.en: What you see: The right atrium and right ventricle dilate with a large coaptation gap between the leaflets. Colour shows a broad systolic jet into the atrium. Severe disease gives a vena contracta of 7 mm or more with an effective orifice of 0.40 sq cm or more. The continuous wave envelope looks dense and triangular with early peaking, and the inferior vena cava dilates with reduced collapse.

Normal values with units: Effective regurgitant orifice. Mild below 0.20 sq cm. Moderate 0.20 to 0.39 sq cm. Severe 0.40 sq cm or more.. Source: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on tricuspid regurgitation quantitation
Vena contracta width. Mild below 3 mm. Moderate 3 to 6.9 mm. Severe 7 mm or more.. Source: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on vena contracta
Right ventricular basal diameter. Normal 42 mm or below in the focused view. Above this the ventricle is dilated.. Source: ASE 2019 transthoracic examination guideline, section on the right ventricle

Inferior vena cava. Above 21 mm with below 50 percent collapse suggests raised right atrial pressure around 15 mmHg.. Source: ASE 2019 transthoracic examination guideline, section on the inferior vena cava

ECG and heart sound correlation ecg: Right atrial enlargement gives tall peaked P waves. An incomplete right bundle branch block pattern appears with volume overload. Atrial fibrillation follows when the right atrium dilates.

ECG and heart sound correlation sounds: A pansystolic murmur at the left lower sternal edge rises with inspiration. A right sided third sound also rises with inspiration. A loud pulmonary component of the second sound marks raised pressure.

What to report: Mechanism: primary leaflet disease against functional annular dilatation with the cause
Effective orifice, vena contracta and envelope shape with the jet velocity
Right heart sizes, annular diameter and vena cava assessment
Pulmonary pressure estimate because it drives functional disease
Red flags needing urgent referral: Severe regurgitation with right heart failure and liver congestion, needs urgent cardiology review
Vegetation on the tricuspid valve with fever, needs urgent endocarditis workup with blood cultures
Severe regurgitation with pulmonary hypertension and syncope, needs urgent pulmonary hypertension review
Pitfalls: Pacemaker leads cross the valve and distort the jet, so note lead position in every device patient.
Respiration swings right sided velocities widely, so average across a calm breath.
Tricuspid disease follows left sided disease and lung disease, so always report the full chain.

todo.en: How to get it on the probe, step by step: Start in the right ventricle focused apical view and include the full right atrium and vena cava.
Measure the tricuspid annulus in diastole and the basal right ventricular diameter.
Map the jet with colour and zoom on the vena contracta at the narrowest neck.
Record continuous wave Doppler parallel to the jet for the peak velocity and envelope shape.
Measure the inferior vena cava with sniff collapse and record hepatic vein flow.

Common mistakes and how to correct them: Measuring the annulus on a foreshortened right ventricle. Fix: Turn the patient further left and slide medially. A rotated cut foreshortens the annulus and hides the gap.
Underreading vena contracta with low colour gain. Fix: Lower the colour scale and raise gain slightly until the full jet borders appear, then measure the neck.
Calling severe primary disease before excluding pulmonary hypertension. Fix: Treat pressure and volume first. Functional regurgitation falls as right ventricular afterload falls.

remember.en: Integrate pulmonary pressure and vena cava findings into the grade.

q.en: Which effective orifice marks severe tricuspid regurgitation?

why.en: Severe is 0.40 sq cm or more with vena contracta 7 mm or more.

q.en: How does the murmur behave on inspiration?

o.en: It radiates to the neck veins

why.en: Inspiration raises venous return to the right heart, so the murmur grows louder.

q.en: A dilated right heart shows a broad jet. What settles mechanism and grade?

o.en: Measure pulmonary pressure and right heart sizes first

why.en: Most disease is functional from raised afterload, so pulmonary pressure and chamber sizes decide management.

q.en: A pacemaker lead crosses the valve through the jet. What do you do?

o.en: Note lead position and reassess the jet around it
Remove the lead at the bedside

why.en: Leads distort jets and can cause regurgitation themselves, so document position and interpret with care.
